summary: TechCrunch's running timeline of Sam Altman's abrupt firing as OpenAI CEO on November 17, 2023, and the days that followed. It covers Greg Brockman's resignation, the employee revolt, the board's talks with Anthropic and Microsoft, Altman's brief move to Microsoft, and the November 21 agreement for Altman to return with a new initial board. It also notes Microsoft gaining a non-voting board observer on November 29.
one_line: A TechCrunch day-by-day timeline of Sam Altman's November 2023 firing from OpenAI, the resignations and employee revolt, and his return as CEO under a new board.
key_facts: OpenAI's board fired Sam Altman, ex-Y Combinator president, as CEO on Friday, November 17, 2023; the company makes ChatGPT, GPT-4 and DALL-E 3.

Greg Brockman, OpenAI's president and co-founder, was removed as board chairman and then resigned; senior researchers Jakub Pachocki (director of research) and Aleksander Madry (head of preparedness) and one other researcher also resigned.
At an all-hands meeting, Ilya Sutskever dismissed claims of a 'hostile takeover' and said the ouster was necessary to protect OpenAI's mission of 'making AI beneficial to humanity.'
OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap wrote in a memo that the board's decision 'was not made in response to malfeasance' and was a 'breakdown in communication between Sam and the board.'
A planned employee share sale led by Thrive Capital, valuing OpenAI at about $86 billion, was reported to be in jeopardy after the firing.
Emmett Shear, co-founder of Twitch, was appointed interim CEO on November 19, replacing Mira Murati, who had briefly been interim CEO.
OpenAI's board approached Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about a merger and about replacing Altman as CEO; Amodei quickly turned down the CEO offer.
On November 20, Altman, Brockman and colleagues announced they would join Microsoft to lead a new AI research team, though Satya Nadella left the door open for other OpenAI staffers.
Ilya Sutskever posted on X, 'I deeply regret my participation in the board's actions,' and said he would do everything he could to reunite the company.
Nearly 500 of OpenAI's roughly 770 employees, including Sutskever, signed a letter threatening to quit unless the board resigned and reappointed Altman; the number later climbed to over 650.
The New York Times reported Altman had tried to push out board member Helen Toner over a paper she co-wrote that he saw as overly critical of OpenAI.
On November 21, OpenAI announced an agreement in principle for Altman to return as CEO with a new initial board of Bret Taylor (Chair), Larry Summers and Adam D'Angelo.
On November 29, OpenAI said Microsoft would get a non-voting observer on the new initial board.
